items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Everybody expects you to sound like Bird Berg, and if you did, you were copying.

ctx.x: Well, I say, like the altos I knew just got out of the service, they switched over to bass. And he

says the reason he switched over to bass, how can he play like that -- and a whole lot of altos had put their horns down because of it. Not really, but they would say, well, what's the use? Everybody expects you to sound like Bird Berg, and if you did, you were copying.

Now there was a whole lot of musicians who hate to copy, you know, the creative musicians. I mean, that wasn't it. Just like, me, speaking about myself, now I loved Blanton, I loved him, and I took a little bit from Blanton, took a little bit from Israel Crosby and I put a little bit of Wilbur Ware in there, so I believe I got my own little way of playing, you know? So that's me. I don't find, like I hear people come up, saying, "You don't sound like so and so and so and so .." and I say, "Yeah, I have to sound…
